experiments.plan.intro: Before running a test: how many units each group needs to detect the effect you care about, and how long that takes at your traffic.
experiments.plan.liftUnit: The effect is a relative lift: 5 means +5 % of the current value.
experiments.plan.pointsUnit: The effect is in percentage points: 1 means 10 % → 11 %.
experiments.plan.incomplete: Give the current value and the effect to detect (and the standard deviation of a mean).
experiments.plan.curveTitle: Units per group and the smallest lift they detect
experiments.plan.curveLabel: Units per group against the smallest detectable lift
experiments.plan.curveNote: Halving the effect to detect needs about four times the units.
experiments.plan.bandit.title: Fixed split vs bandit
experiments.plan.bandit.intro: The planned test simulated 200 times: once with the fixed split, once with a bandit that moves traffic to the variant that looks best, day after day.
experiments.plan.bandit.sure: Sure of the best at the end
experiments.plan.bandit.chartTitle: Cumulative regret over the test, simulated

experiments.policy.why: A short rule that gives each unit the variant that suits it, learnt from the columns describing the units and measured by cross-validation against giving everyone one variant.
experiments.policy.caveat: Hypothesis to confirm with a new test: the rule is learnt on this test's units, and the columns it reads must be measured before the test, not changed by it.

experiments.policy.valuesNote: Cross-validated value per unit, 95 % bootstrap interval; the dotted line is everyone on {best} ({value}).
experiments.policy.valuesLabel: Value of the rule and of each variant given to everyone, with their intervals

module.segments.label: Segments
segments.title: Segments
segments.description: Groups of similar rows, found and described for you, and rows unlike the others. The app picks the columns, prepares them and chooses how many segments hold up.
segments.first: Finding segments with the app's choices…
segments.runCompare.hint: Tick 2 to 5 runs to compare them
segments.sampledNote: Fitted on a reproducible sample of {rows} rows; every other row went to its nearest segment.
segments.scoresHelp: Each k from 2 to 10 is tried. Silhouette: how much closer rows are to their own segment than to the next one (−1 to 1). Calinski–Harabasz: spread between segments over spread within. Davies–Bouldin: how much segments overlap (lower is better). Inertia: spread within segments; the elbow is where adding a segment stops helping. The dotted line is the k kept.
segments.notGrouped: Rows HDBSCAN did not place in any group: too far from every dense region.
segments.mapPcaHelp: The prepared rows projected on their two principal components; the share of the variance each one explains is in the axis title. Diamonds are the segments' centres.
segments.mapTsneHelp: t-SNE keeps neighbours together; the distances between groups and their sizes do not mean much.
segments.profilesHelp: One line per column: the mean (numbers) or the most frequent category with its share. Highlighted cells differ strongly from the whole (standardised gap of 0.8 or more).
segments.profilesNote: In the columns' own units, on the rows the segments were fitted on.
segments.stabilityHelp: The same method is refitted on 10 subsamples of 80 % of the rows and compared with these segments (adjusted Rand index: 1 = the same groups, 0 = no better than chance). Below 0.6 the segments are not stable.
segments.dendrogramNote: Ward's tree on {rows} rows, cut (dashed line) where the segments are.
segments.saveHint: A new dataset with the same rows (filtered as they were) and a segment column; it opens in Compare, KPI, ML and Time series. The source is not changed.
segments.agreementHelp: Agreement: adjusted Rand index between two runs' segments, on the rows they share (1 = the same groups).
segments.wordsHint: The words each segment's texts use more than the others
segments.derivedHint: Measures of the text columns and options of the lists of choices, added only when ticked.
segments.columnsHint: The ML preparation rules with the distance profile: every number scaled robustly, categories one-hot (20 at most). Changes apply to both sections.
unusual.methodHelp.auto: Robust Mahalanobis on a few roughly elliptical numbers, Isolation Forest otherwise.
unusual.methodHelp.isolation_forest: 200 trees cut the rows apart; unusual rows are isolated in few cuts.
unusual.methodHelp.mahalanobis: Distance from the centre, taking correlations into account, with a robust covariance (MCD). Numbers only: among categories, it reads the numbers when there are at least 3.
unusual.methodHelp.lof: Rows isolated in their own neighbourhood, even if normal elsewhere.
unusual.segmentFrom: Measured from the latest segmentation ({run} segments).
unusual.columnsAuto: Same columns and preparation as Segments (automatic).
unusual.columnsCustom: Same columns and preparation as Segments (your choices).

unusual.headline: {rows} unusual rows of {of}
unusual.sampled: Fitted on a reproducible sample of {rows} rows; every row was scored.
unusual.curveHelp: Each row's score, sorted. The proposed threshold sits where the curve breaks (steep, then flat), else at the 1 % most unusual rows. Move it with the slider or click the curve: the rows follow without scoring again.
unusual.listedNote: The {rows} most unusual rows are listed with their reasons; the threshold moves among them.
unusual.percentile: {share} % of rows are at or below (median {median})
tsm.sarimax.what: The automatic ARIMA's orders, found without drivers, then refitted with the drivers as regressors (regression with ARIMA errors). Without drivers it is the automatic ARIMA.
ts.drivers.title: Drivers
ts.drivers.usedBy: Used by SARIMAX, Linear regression and Gradient boosting; the other models ignore them.
ts.drivers.explain: Outside variables that may explain the series, summed or averaged per period like it (a yes/no column becomes the share of rows that are yes). Known in advance: you give their future values. Past only: they enter lagged by the horizon, so nothing from the future leaks in.
ts.drivers.lagged: Enters lagged by {lag} periods (the horizon): no future value needed.
ts.drivers.lastWarn: The last value is repeated: this assumes it stays flat.
ts.drivers.flagHint: 0/1 flag, known in advance: future rows of the file, 0 where there is none.
ts.drivers.none: No other numeric or yes/no column to use.
ts.drivers.noModel: None of the chosen models uses drivers.
ts.drivers.suggest: {what} and {name} move together (r = {r} between their changes): use {name} as a driver.
ts.drivers.resultsHint: Each driver model was scored again without each driver, on the same rolling origins. A driver helps when the MASE is at least 5 % lower with it; within 5 % the gain is unclear.
ts.groups.title: Every group
ts.groups.countLimited: {n} {group} values · the {limit} largest on their own
ts.groups.global: Global model (one gradient boosting over every series)

ts.groups.progress: Progress of the forecast of every group
ts.groups.stage.global: Training the global model on every series…
